after.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $f(t)=12({t}^{2}-t)$ onto the subspace spanned by $g(t)=t-1.$
after.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $f(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{g(t)}$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t)=\frac{⟨f(t),g(t)⟩}{⟨g(t),g(t)⟩}\,g(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),g(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}12({t}^{2}-t)\cdot (t-1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(12{t}^{3}-24{t}^{2}+12t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =[3{t}^{4}-8{t}^{3}+6{t}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(3-8+6)-0 \\  & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨g(t),g(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(t-1)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}-2t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}+t]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}-1+1)-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the projection is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t) & =\frac{⟨f(t),g(t)⟩}{⟨g(t),g(t)⟩}\,g(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{3})}\cdot (t-1) \\  & =3(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$
